goal: stale or ambiguous work never becomes a new authorized effect through retry, crash or takeover
authoring_boundary: provider-free design only; no run, replay, host, store or provider action is authorized by this file

oracle_labels.out_of_scope: RefValid(log) == OUT_OF_SCOPE when committed events exceed 20
oracle_labels.projection: RefProject(log) fixed 16-field tuple; [1] ordinal, [2] tail, [3] status, [8] attempt, [9] paused, [12] result value, [14] effect status, [15] timer status
oracle_labels.bridge: trace_checker.check_trace reports first_divergence_index against observed_state_digest / observed_projection

injected_schedule: crash before the canonical admission/append of the logical operation
restart and retry the same logical operation under the same attempt identity
retry identical command bytes, then attempt a structurally valid but distinct identity
observation_oracle: RefValid(log) over the finite prefix: no committed event for a pre-admission crash
RefState(log).ordinal and .tail unchanged by the retry
RefState(log).receipts contains zero entries for the failed identity
fixtures.decidable_predicate: For the finite schedule, the committed-event count and effect count for the logical operation are both zero before admission and remain zero under identical-identity retry; a distinct identity is refused by the authority checks rather than admitted as new work.

injected_schedule: admit the operation and commit the atomic PrepareEffect batch (EffectPrepared + OutboxEnqueued)
crash after the batch is durable but before MarkDispatch
restart and re-present the prepared intent with the same token; then attempt a second PrepareEffect
observation_oracle: RefState(log).effect.status is ES_PREPARED and not ES_INFLIGHT
RefState(log).outbox length is one for the stable token
RefState(log).receipts id count is one per logical operation
fixtures.decidable_predicate: The prepared intent is either re-presented for dispatch or held without mutation; no receiver effect occurs; a second PrepareEffect for the same token does not create a second intent identity or exceed outbox capacity 2.

injected_schedule: crash at the canonical commit/ack boundary before the acknowledgement is durable
restart, replay the retained prefix, and re-query the same operation identity
separately, crash after a durable acknowledgement and replay the retained committed prefix
observation_oracle: RefValid(log) over the replay equal to VALID_BOUNDED for the acknowledged prefix
RefState(log).ordinal, .tail and .receipts equal between the live pre-crash fold and the replayed fold when the commit was acknowledged
RefProject(log)[1] and [2] bind the same ordinal and tail
fixtures.decidable_predicate: An acknowledged canonical commit replays to the identical reference state under the declared durability profile; an unacknowledged commit remains unknown and is not reported as durable success.

injected_schedule: commit MarkDispatch and crash at dispatch-intent publication before receiver acceptance
restart and retry the same operation, then retry with changed bytes under the same id
attempt automatic writer takeover while the dispatch outcome is ambiguous
observation_oracle: RefState(log).effect.status is ES_INFLIGHT or ES_UNKNOWN, never ES_SUCCEEDED without an observation
RefState(log).outbox no longer holds the dispatched token
RefState(log).receipts id count remains one; a changed-body duplicate under the same id is COMMAND_CONFLICT
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Before receiver acceptance no mutation is counted; the reservation stays held; a retry does not mint a new effect identity; changed bytes under the same command id conflict rather than admit.

injected_schedule: receiver mutates once, then the response is lost before the receiver receipt is recorded
restart and retry the same operation and attempt
reconcile a late authoritative receipt for the same effect identity
observation_oracle: Independent receiver mutation count for the logical operation equals one
RefState(log).effect.status is ES_UNKNOWN until reconciliation, then ES_SUCCEEDED for the same token
RefState(log).receipts id is stable across the retry; no second effect id
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A lost pre-receipt response yields at most one receiver mutation; retry reconciles the original identity; reconciliation settles that effect and does not repeat it or release the held liability twice.

injected_schedule: dispatch and receiver acceptance succeed, then the reply is lost after dispatch
retry the same operation under the same command identity across a process/writer change
inject a stale fenced request and an unrelated competing retry owner
observation_oracle: Independent receiver mutation count is one for the stable operation
RefState(log).attempt does not increase without the semantic owner admitting a new attempt
RefValid(log) stays VALID_BOUNDED across the retry prefix
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A post-dispatch reply loss leaves exactly one effect and holds its liability; only the declared semantic retry owner can admit a new attempt; a stale fenced request causes no mutation.

injected_schedule: delay writer A before the receiver gate while canonical revocation is already recorded
keep receiver-fence installation pending and inspect its status
persist installed floor 8 and acknowledge installation; then attempt stale epoch 7 writer A and valid epoch 8 writer B
crash and restart at each cut, retrying request and install with stable ids
observation_oracle: Independent durable installed floor equals 8 and never regresses
Independent receiver mutation ledger shows zero epoch-7 mutations after install
RefProject(log)[1] and [2] bind the accepted canonical order across restart
fixtures.decidable_predicate: After the floor-8 gate is installed and acknowledged, no epoch-7 mutation occurs including across restart; pre-install exposure stays pending/unknown; an invalid issuer or fabricated higher floor is refused; no check-to-effect race admits stale work.

injected_schedule: attempt a stale epoch-7 mutation after the installed-current fence
attempt a lower floor and a fabricated higher floor from an unqualified issuer
crash and restart the receiver between the install acknowledgement and the stale attempt
observation_oracle: Independent receiver mutation ledger shows zero accepted stale mutations
Durable installed floor is monotonic across restart
RefState(log) contains no witnessing receipt for the stale attempt
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Any epoch below the installed-current floor is refused at the receiver; the floor never regresses; an unqualified issuer cannot lower or raise the floor; restart does not heal stale work authority.

injected_schedule: place an old epoch-7 dispatch before floor 8 is installed while canonical revocation is already recorded
leave fence installation pending and classify the exposure interval
install floor 8 and separately observe a later stale attempt
observation_oracle: Independent receiver ledger labels the pre-install mutation as prior exposure
RefState(log).effect.status distinguishes pre-install unknown exposure from post-install rejection
RefProject(log)[14] effect status is never promoted to ES_KNOWN_NO_EFFECT from a missing observation
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A mutation placed before the installed-current fence is recorded as prior or pending exposure, never erased; that exposure interval is distinct from a stale-after-install acceptance, which must be refused.

injected_schedule: root owns a worker, shell, monitor and relauncher; a borrowed consultant owns an unrelated operation
invoke Aggressive Stop at a dispatch cut
discover a late descendant after the stop scope is computed
attempt a late relaunch of a stopped selected actor
observation_oracle: Independent per-member target set for Aggressive excludes descendants unless separately selected
RefState(log) shows no new admission for the stopped selected actor
Unrelated borrowed operation retains its own receipt and liability
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Aggressive Stop affects only the selected actor; it does not silently include descendants or the unrelated borrowed operation, and no late relaunch creates a new authorized effect.

injected_schedule: root owns worker, shell, monitor and relauncher; a borrowed consultant owns an unrelated operation; one remote member is unreachable
invoke Full Stop and then discover a late owned descendant
leave the remote member without a life signal
observation_oracle: Independent ownership graph enumerates every rooted member
RefState(log) shows no new rooted admission or relaunch
Unreachable member is unresolved with held liability, not stopped
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Full Stop closes rooted admission and replaces/accounts for every discovered owned member while preserving the unrelated borrowed operation; the unreachable member remains unknown, so a drained or quiescent claim is not made.

injected_schedule: Lazy Stop is requested and the work never reaches the named next-operation boundary before its deadline
cancel acknowledgement returns while the effect remains unresolved
a remote member does not report within the bounded observation window
observation_oracle: RefState(log) shows the named boundary or an unresolved status, never observed-stopped without boundary evidence
Independent per-member receipt truth separates requested, accepted, fenced and observed
Unreachable member retains held liability
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Lazy Stop reports the named boundary, deadline or timeout; it never produces observed-stopped without boundary or quiescence evidence; an unreachable member remains unknown rather than stopped.

injected_schedule: effect commits and the reply is lost, then a cancellation acknowledgement arrives
late valid historical receiver receipt arrives for the original incarnation
a wrong-incarnation receipt arrives for the same nominal operation
observation_oracle: RefState(log).effect.status is ES_UNKNOWN until an authoritative observation, never rolled back by a cancel ack
Receipt binding distinguishes original admission identity from the wrong incarnation
RefProject(log)[12] result value is unchanged by the cancel acknowledgement
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A cancellation acknowledgement is not terminal success and not rollback; a late valid receipt classifies only the original operation; a wrong-incarnation receipt is rejected; neither restores a permit.

injected_schedule: deliver one command to a replacement holder across writer and lease epoch changes
retry identical command bytes with the same id
retry changed bytes under the same id, and retry a stale lease under the old epoch
observation_oracle: RefState(log).receipts returns one receipt per stable command id for equal bytes
RefValid(log) reports COMMAND_CONFLICT / DET_COMMAND_DIGEST for changed bytes under the same id
RefProject(log)[1] ordinal does not advance for a cached duplicate
fixtures.decidable_predicate: An identical duplicate returns the original receipt without a second committed event; changed bytes under the same id conflict; a stale lease epoch refuses rather than start a new semantic operation.

injected_schedule: produce each partial outcome in turn: locally saved only, canonical accepted undispatched, transport delivered, receiver accepted, applied, observed business outcome, settled
variant where the process exits after dispatch with no further receipt
variant with a wrong-operation or wrong-payload receipt and a timeout with possible application
observation_oracle: RefProject(log) fields [3] status, [12] result value and [14] effect status are read without collapsing to a single success flag
RefState(log).receipts preserve the stage boundary of each supplied receipt
A missing later-stage receipt leaves the corresponding projection field unresolved
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Each supplied receipt is labelled with its stage and what it cannot establish; no transport acknowledgement or process exit changes applied, rollback or settled from unknown; a wrong-binding receipt stays quarantined; a timeout preserves uncertainty and held liability.

injected_schedule: inject a crash-time meter report equal to raw zero, then an explicit absent report, a malformed unit and a stale reading
supply one complete independently witnessed no-call report
resolve an uncertain liability partly to measured usage and release only the proven remainder
attempt a calendar-day rollover without authorized budget renewal
observation_oracle: A raw crash-zero is retained as raw and its validated value is null with reason crash_incomplete_meter
Only a complete witnessed no-call report yields a known zero
Conserved totals: settled plus outstanding plus withheld plus proposed stays within the gross limit
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A raw crash-time zero is not validated as actual usage; absent, stale or malformed reports remain null with a reason; an uncertain liability is held exactly once; day rollover and repeated recovery cannot reset the allowance.

injected_schedule: lose an effect acknowledgement, replace the node, then attempt to release and re-reserve the same liability
ingest a late authoritative settlement and replay a duplicate cumulative meter
attempt to count one uncertainty as both an outstanding reservation and a separate liability total
observation_oracle: Independent typed-unit ledger arithmetic over reservation and settlement identities
Settled and outstanding remain disjoint; uncertain liability is annotated once
RefState(log).effect.status does not settle without an authoritative observation
fixtures.decidable_predicate: The unresolved liability stays attached exactly once across replacement and recovery; recovery moves withheld allowance into outstanding without changing the conserved total; only a supported authoritative settlement changes status; a duplicate cumulative meter does not double-count.

injected_schedule: deliver the same eligible occurrence twice concurrently with identical bytes
deliver an altered payload under the same occurrence key
deliver an expired occurrence plus a manual trigger/backfill path under a revoked generation
observation_oracle: An independent key-to-payload and receipt map
RefState(log).receipts id count equals one for identical eligible occurrences
RefValid(log) reports COMMAND_CONFLICT for altered bytes under the same key
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Exactly one logical admission occurs for identical eligible occurrences and the original receipt is returned; conflicting, expired, superseded or Stop-fenced occurrences yield zero new admissions; manual and backfill paths traverse the identical current authority checks.

injected_schedule: one operation with a three-attempt semantic bound; scheduler, adapter and SDK each propose a retry at the same failure barrier
lose the acknowledgement after the receiver accepts attempt one
provide a known-no-effect transient failure positive control
remove the adapter retry visibility and attempt to compound retries
observation_oracle: Independent operation-attempt receiver registry distinguishes transport duplicates from new semantic attempts
RefState(log).attempt never exceeds the declared bound
RefState(log).receipts id remains the original identity for a reconciled lost acknowledgement
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Only the declared semantic retry owner admits a new attempt; the combined attempt and liability total stays within the bound; a lost acknowledgement reconciles the original identity rather than creating a new effect; a missing nested retry upper bound refuses the bounded profile.

injected_schedule: lose writer W1 and let the plugin acquire a fresh writer fence and committed prefix when the declared availability condition holds
submit the old writer and let the current writer append across every takeover cut
remove the required availability condition and attempt both sides
restore an old backup and membership and toggle the plugin off to inspect core-only status
observation_oracle: Independent accepted-write order and writer-fence register
RefValid(log) over the accepted prefix; stale appends refuse
Separate receiver work-epoch oracle unchanged by writer takeover
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Takeover admits exactly one accepted writer and only after required fencing evidence; stale appends and unsafe partition commits refuse; an unavailable fence yields honest unavailable/unknown rather than dual authority; writer takeover never revives stale workers, effects or Stop grants.

injected_schedule: within an authorized local session, cut at declared commit boundaries using the specified abrupt reset, bounded and non-destructive first
replay the retained committed prefix and receiver floors and compare to the independent pre-fault ledger
observe spawn, Stop and relauncher containment separately on the exact profile
observation_oracle: Independent pre-fault committed-state and fence ledger equals the post-reset replay
RefState(log) replay against RefValid(log) is identical
Fault-triggered evidence is true; a substitute mechanism does not qualify
fixtures.decidable_predicate: Within the declared fault model, acknowledged committed state and monotonic fences survive the cut and replay identically; if the required native mechanism or authorization is absent the fixture is blocked, not passed by a substitute.

injected_schedule: deliver a duplicate spawn intent before the launch receipt arrives
launch occurs and the acknowledgement is lost, then the controller restarts
retry the same spawn identity and attempt a changed-bytes duplicate
observation_oracle: An independent launch-intent and process-incarnation register
RefState(log).receipts id count is one for the stable spawn identity
RefValid(log) reports COMMAND_CONFLICT for changed bytes under the same id
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A duplicate spawn intent before its receipt does not launch twice; a lost acknowledgement does not create a new incarnation or effect identity; controller restart reconciles the original spawn rather than launching a blind duplicate.

injected_schedule: interrupt a stream so it produces no result, while an alternate crash-result variant explicitly reports zeroed usage and cost
lose the reply before the receiver receipt is recorded
attempt cancellation and then supply delayed effect evidence through a permitted reconciliation channel
observation_oracle: An explicit zeroed report is retained as raw; validated usage is null with a reason
RefState(log).attempt and .retry_ready reflect reconciliation, not a blind restart
RefProject(log)[12] result value stays unresolved until a valid observation
fixtures.decidable_predicate: An interrupted stream with no result holds its liability and reports unknown, never zero usage; an explicitly zeroed crash report is not adopted as actual usage; a delayed valid observation settles the original operation only.

injected_schedule: a queued follow-up survives a generic native abort
a cancel acknowledgement arrives before a late tool/update/result for the same operation
a pending approval reconnects and an old-epoch response returns
observation_oracle: An independent per-operation receipt binding distinguishes the current epoch from the old epoch
RefState(log).effect.status is unaffected by a prior cancel acknowledgement
RefValid(log) rejects the old-epoch response binding
fixtures.decidable_predicate: A cancel acknowledgement does not become terminal success and does not roll back an unresolved effect; a queued follow-up survives a generic abort without inheriting stale authority; an old-epoch response is not adopted for the pending approval.

injected_schedule: partition one node and permit only pre-admitted bounded local computation and spooling
attempt new offline work, renewal, child spawn and effect dispatch
advance current authority, reconnect, and submit old observations and requests
reconcile duplicate and conflicting observations with exact provenance
observation_oracle: An independent canonical authority trace and scoped receiver dispatch log
Old observations remain historical and deduplicated in RefState(log).receipts
Stale post-reconnect work is refused by the current authority checks
fixtures.decidable_predicate: No offline spool entry becomes a canonical grant or new authorized effect; reconnect does not revive stale permits; duplicate observations deduplicate and conflicts quarantine rather than overwrite.

injected_schedule: return a task handle, then expire it while its synthetic effect remains observable elsewhere
return completed with an error flag for the same operation
race a drain against an in-flight member that is unreachable at the deadline
observation_oracle: The synthetic effect remains observable and its liability stays held after TTL expiry
RefProject(log)[3] status distinguishes a completed protocol exchange from a failed tool-level outcome
An unreachable in-flight member prevents a drained or quiescent projection
fixtures.decidable_predicate: TTL expiry preserves uncertainty and the reservation rather than releasing budget or declaring failure; a completed-with-error exchange is a completed protocol exchange with a failed tool outcome and no verified-goal success; an unreachable in-flight member blocks a drained claim.
